title: Dapr in Container Apps, and when the abstraction pays off

videos.script: Lesson 8 put the shop in Container Apps. This lesson puts a second process beside it, called Dapr. {{sidecar}} Dapr runs next to your program and answers on localhost. Your code asks it to save a value or publish a message. Dapr does the talking to Redis, or to Service Bus. In Container Apps it is one setting, and Azure adds the sidecar to every replica. {{laptop}} You will run it on your laptop with Docker, beside the shop's image, inside the shop's own network. {{components}} Then two components, written as YAML files. A state store and a broker, both on Redis. Two programs subscribe to the shop's orders, and each one gets its own copy. {{swap}} Then the swap. The broker becomes Microsoft's Service Bus emulator, and the code does not change. It still fails once, and the reason is worth knowing. And afterwards each order reaches only one of the two programs. {{cost}} Last, the bill. An extra container in every replica, an extra hop on every call, and a second log to read. You will measure two of those, and decide when the trade pays.
